- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.text:
Rule 1 satisfied: 6 passing, 3 todo.

**Naming Evaluation (first priority)**

- `nextGeneration` — accurately names the domain concept. Keep.
- `isNeighbor` — accurate. But note it exists only to power `countLiveNeighbors`, which scans *all* cells to find neighbors. `neighborsOf` already generates the 8 neighbor coordinates directly. This is **conceptual duplication** (Rule 3): "what does adjacency mean" is expressed twice, once as a predicate over a pair and once as a coordinate generator.
- `candidates` — vague. Candidates *for what*? Rename to `cellsToEvaluate`.
- `isSame` — fine, but it duplicates the inline comparison in `isAlive` (`other[0] === cell[0] && other[1] === cell[1]`). Rule 3 violation.
- `survives` — misleading for the reproduction case: a dead cell coming to life does not "survive". Rename to `isAliveNextGeneration`.

**APP mass before** (per-component, summed across the module):

| Function | Const | Bind | Invoke | Cond | Loop | Assign | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `isNeighbor` | 3 | 4 | 4 (2 abs, 2 −) → 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 15 |
| `countLiveNeighbors` | 0 | 2 | 3 → 6 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 13 |
| `isAlive` | 4 | 2 | 1 → 2 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 13 |
| `neighborsOf` | 8 | 4 | 3 → 6 | 1 → 4 | 10 | 0 | 32 |
| `candidates` | 1 | 4 | 3 → 6 | 0 | 15 | 0 | 26 |
| `isSame` | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| `survives` | 2 | 3 | 2 → 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 13 |
| `nextGeneration` | 0 | 2 | 3 → 6 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 13 |

**Total mass: 129**

The prompt asks whether a Set-keyed representation improves clarity. It does, and it dissolves the duplication: with a `Set<string>` of `"x,y"` keys, `isAlive` becomes a lookup, dedup in `candidates` becomes free, and `isNeighbor`/`isSame` disappear entirely because `neighborsOf` becomes the single definition of adjacency.

Let me apply this as one refactoring.

content.text: Green — 6 passing, 3 todo, same as before. Let me also confirm the types are clean.

Typecheck clean.

**APP mass after:**

| Function | Const | Bind | Invoke | Cond | Loop | Assign | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keyOf` | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| `cellOf` | 1 | 4 | 2 → 4 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 14 |
| `neighborsOf` | 8 | 4 | 3 → 6 | 1 → 4 | 10 | 0 | 32 |
| `countLiveNeighbors` | 0 | 3 | 4 → 8 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 16 |
| `cellsToEvaluate` | 0 | 3 | 5 → 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | 23 |
| `isAliveNextGeneration` | 2 | 3 | 4 → 8 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 17 |
| `nextGeneration` | 0 | 3 | 5 → 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | 23 |

**Total mass: 129 → 129 (Δ 0)**

Mass is a wash — the Set machinery (`keyOf`, `cellOf`) costs about what the deleted `isNeighbor`/`isSame` scans returned. The win is entirely on Rule 2 and Rule 3, which outrank APP.

**Refactoring applied** (one change, tests green throughout):

- **Rule 3, duplication removed.** Adjacency was defined twice: `isNeighbor` (Chebyshev-distance predicate over a pair) and `neighborsOf` (offset generator). `countLiveNeighbors` now asks `neighborsOf` for the 8 coordinates and checks membership, so `neighborsOf` is the single source of truth for what "neighbor" means. `isNeighbor` deleted. Likewise `isSame` and the inline coordinate comparison inside `isAlive` were the same knowledge twice — both dissolve into `Set.has(keyOf(cell))`, so `isSame` and `isAlive` are deleted too. Four helpers became two.
- **Rule 2, naming.** `candidates` → `cellsToEvaluate` ("candidates for what?" is now answered). `survives` → `isAliveNextGeneration`, because a dead cell brought to life by reproduction does not "survive" — the old name contradicted the branch it guarded, which is exactly the case the last Green phase added.
- **Rule 2, clarity of the dedup.** The old `candidates` used `all.findIndex(...) === index`, an index-identity idiom the reader has to decode. It is now `[...new Set(keys)]`, which states deduplication directly.
- **Incidental:** the linear scans in the prompt (`isAlive`, `countLiveNeighbors`, dedup) are now O(1) lookups against the live set. Not the motivation — the duplication was — but it follows from the same change.

Exported signature `nextGeneration(cells: Cell[]): Cell[]` and `Cell` are unchanged. `CellKey`/`keyOf`/`cellOf` are module-private.

**Not done, deliberately:** the three `it.todo` tests (block still life, both blinker phases) are untouched — no implementing ahead. I also left `neighborsOf` as-is despite it being the heaviest function (mass 32); a flat literal array of the 8 offsets would cut mass, but the nested-loop form makes the "all 8 surrounding cells, excluding self" rule visible, and Rule 2 outranks APP.

One caveat worth flagging for the next phase: `cellOf` round-trips through `split(",").map(Number)`, which is correct for negative coordinates (`"-1,1"` parses fine) — relevant because the pending blinker tests expect `(-1,1)`. I verified this holds by typecheck and by the existing tests only, not by a new test, since writing one would be implementing ahead.
